Assets.NotesMarkdown:
# Backoffice 1.0.100

1. Fixed: after "Restart to update" the app no longer shows a crash notice at the next start.
2. The TradeNextFX logo mark and app icon are the brand's own artwork; the top-left header and the bottom-left status line show the logo mark with the name in the brand's own two colours.
3. Each broker's app keeps its own saved sign-ins and settings, so apps from different brokers on one PC never share them. Settings has an Uninstall option that also removes this app's saved data (ticked by default).
4. Dealing chart: zoom in much further, solid crisp candles, follows the live edge, one clean menu style, crisp drawing tools, and easier-to-pick position lines and tags with a red close cross on hover and a highlighted selection.

Assets.NotesMarkdown:
# Backoffice 1.0.101

Symbols tab

1. Trading hours are set in one clear editor: seven day rows, each with its own windows (add and remove), trade and quote hours on separate tabs, and presets (FX week, 24/7, Metals, Indices, Crypto) that come from TradeNextFX. A preview shows the week in the broker's time and in your own time. Overlapping windows are marked at the row, and a window that runs past midnight splits into two days by itself. Empty means the default FX week.
2. The price feed screen now shows API ping, Feed delay and Last tick, each coloured green under 5 seconds, amber under 30 seconds and red beyond. The Symbols screen shows the same two figures, and a Last tick column.
3. The Symbols list has more columns, hidden by default and switched on from COLUMNS: default book, tick size, tick value, margin and profit currency, execution mode, fill policy, swap type, triple swap day, freeze level, initial and maintenance margin rates, description, display order, price source and last tick. A value that is not set reads "Not set". Allowed sides is now Trade mode (Full, Long only, Short only, Close only). These settings can be edited in the table or from the new Settings dialog, and are saved together with the rest.
4. Change several symbols at once: tick them, press CHANGE SELECTED, and set enabled or disabled, markup, swaps, max volume or trading hours in one dialog. The result lists every symbol with the reason when one could not be changed.
5. Add a symbol, clone an existing one (every setting and its trading hours are copied), export the table to CSV (every column that is shown, raw numbers) and import a CSV. An import first shows what it would do for each row, with the reason for any row it would refuse, and writes nothing until you confirm.
6. The right-hand panel for a symbol is split into Pricing, Trading, Swaps, Margin and Sessions. The price source shows each liquidity provider and whether it is on.
7. The Hours column shows TradeNextFX's own summary of the week, for example "Mon-Fri 24h · break 17-18 NY".
8. Display order: Move up and Move down in the symbol menu set the order of the symbol list that traders see.
9. Every refusal shows its reason where you clicked: a missing permission names the permission, and a rejected value names the field and the rule.
10. Symbols: drag a row up or down to set the display order traders see (Move up and Move down stay for the keyboard). Contract size and base and quote currency are shown as columns and in the symbol panel.
11. A liquidity provider's name can be changed from the Pricing section of the symbol panel (Admins only); the symbol list updates at once.
12. Switching between dark and light now repaints the whole window at once; no part keeps the old theme until the pointer passes over it.

Order ticket

13. One order ticket for the whole platform. The ORDER TICKET tab in a client's page is now the same ticket traders use, bound to that client's account: market, limit and stop orders, lots, stop loss and take profit, risk % and the margin the order needs, from the client's own leverage and balance. Only the symbols the client's group may trade are offered. Every send asks you to confirm first, and a refusal shows its reason right under the buttons.
14. In the Dealing screen, right-click a client's position in the Hedge manager and choose Order ticket to open the same ticket for that client at the side of the screen. Close, Modify and the other entries stay where they were. The entry is off, with the reason, when your role may not trade for clients.
15. Manual position (Admins only): the ticket has a MANUAL tab. Type the open price and TradeNextFX fills Open time with the last time the symbol traded at that price, with the date and time down to the second shown as it is (for example 29 Oct 2026 14:05:00) and a note when the time is only known to the minute or the hour. You can edit the time to the second yourself; once you have, a later price never overwrites it, and "use the price's time" fills it again. When the price is not in the history, the ticket says so and lets you set the time yourself. The confirm shows the final open price and time, says it is a manual position, and shows the floating profit and loss and the margin level after, as worked out by TradeNextFX.

Updates, live data and the dealer queue

16. When TradeNextFX marks a version as no longer supported, the app updates itself before you can sign in or work, with a progress bar. If the update server cannot be reached the screen says so and offers Retry.
17. Groups, symbols, staff and liquidity providers are live: one created, renamed or removed shows in every open list and picker (Change group, new account, approvals, symbol lists, staff and provider lists) within a second, with no restart and no refresh, and they are read again after any reconnect.
18. Dealer queue: every waiting row shows how long is left (for example 0:42, red in the last 10 seconds). When it reaches zero the row says Expired and its Accept, Offer new price, Reject and Withdraw buttons are off; the row leaves when TradeNextFX withdraws the order. An accept that arrives too late says "This offer expired".

Stop loss and take profit

19. Stop loss and take profit can be set as an amount in the account currency: the client ORDER TICKET and Change stop loss / take profit offer Price, Pips or Amount for each level, and Live exposure shows an amount as money (stop loss red, take profit blue). The Amount choice appears only once the server supports it for that account; a refusal shows the server's reason in the window.

Settings

20. Settings: "Requote expires after (s)" (default 60) and "Offer expires after (s)" (default 300) set how long a requote and a dealer offer stay open. An Admin changes them (10 to 86400 seconds), they are saved on the server and audited, and anyone else sees the values with the reason they cannot change them. A refused value shows the reason in the window.

Header, Dealing and sign-in

21. The status blocks at the top right are as wide as their text. The SERVER block is exactly as wide as its longest word (Connected, Reconnecting, Disconnected or the link-lost badge), so the header never moves when the connection changes. Spacing around the other blocks is tighter.
22. The Dealing chart's SELL / BUY strip has the same look as the trader terminal's: no box behind it, the same buttons, and it sits in its own strip above the chart so no candle is under it. It collapses to a slim bar, and your choice is remembered.
23. On the sign-in card, "UPDATE AVAILABLE" has its own line under the logo instead of sitting beside it.

Assets.NotesMarkdown:
# Backoffice 1.0.102

Dealing

1. The one-click SELL / BUY strip on the Dealing chart is now the same as in the terminal: the SELL button with its red border, the lot stepper, the BUY button with its blue border and the 1-CLICK switch, with the price line (open, high, low, close) on the same row. There is no panel behind it and no line under it, and the candles start directly below.
2. Dealer P/L, Book P/L and Hedge account P/L, and every P/L figure in the hedge manager and the hedge account, now follow the live prices, the way the terminal's floating P/L does. The figures change in place, profit in blue and loss in red; money already realized stays as TradeNextFX reports it.
3. The hedge buttons (NEW HEDGE ORDER, HEDGE ALL and the HEDGE button on each row) use the brand accent of TradeNextFX.

CRM

4. The Leads pipeline always finishes loading: it shows the leads, or one short line saying it could not load (also when the server is slow or sends something that is not a lead list), instead of staying on "Loading".

Header

5. The SERVER block at the top is as wide as its longest status (Connected, Reconnecting, Disconnected and the link-lost badge), so no other item in the header moves when the status changes.

Reports

6. The STATEMENT button and chip use the brand accent of TradeNextFX, in the light and the dark theme.

Clients

7. The hedge account can be funded and its leverage changed from the backoffice, by a broker admin: Funds shows Deposit, Withdrawal, Adjustment and History for it (no Credit, no Transfer), and Change leverage is in its menu. Each one asks one line first that names the hedge account. A manager or support user still sees only its history and statement, and the group, trading rights, risk limits and the other write items stay hidden for it.

3. The hedge buttons (NEW HEDGE ORDER, HEDGE ALL and the HEDGE button on each row) use the brand accent of TradeNextFX.

CRM

4. The Leads pipeline always finishes loading: it shows the leads, or one short line saying it could not load (also when the server is slow or sends something that is not a lead list), instead of staying on "Loading".

Header

Reports

6. The STATEMENT button and chip use the brand accent of TradeNextFX, in the light and the dark theme.

Clients

7. The hedge account can be funded and its leverage changed from the backoffice, by a broker admin: Funds shows Deposit, Withdrawal, Adjustment and History for it (no Credit, no Transfer), and Change leverage is in its menu. Each one asks one line first that names the hedge account. A manager or support user still sees only its history and statement, and the group, trading rights, risk limits and the other write items stay hidden for it.

# Backoffice 1.0.105

Header

1. The top bar takes less room: its cells are as wide as their text. The connection status keeps the width of its longest message, so nothing shifts when it changes.

Dealing

2. The O H L C values are back in the chart's top row, centred between the timeframes and INDICATORS / SESSIONS / DRAW. On a narrow window, where that row has no room for them, they stay in the one-click strip below it.
3. Waiting orders is tighter and looks like the other tables: lower rows, the standard column headers and rules, striped rows, and smaller row buttons.
4. The Hedge manager no longer leaves an empty strip under its last line when a hedged client position appears.
5. Book positions is back, at the bottom left: every open position of every dealing-group account, in the standard table, with the row menu (Hedge, Unhedge, Order ticket). Waiting orders stays beside it on the right. When you accept a waiting order, the new position appears at once in Book positions as open, and in the Hedge manager as not hedged, ready to hedge or close. Reset layout restores the sizes of both.

KYC

6. KYC opens on the tab with pending checks. Trader's Room submissions are under CLIENT PORTAL, so when only that tab has work, KYC now opens there instead of on an empty list. A tab you pick yourself stays picked.

Stop loss and take profit

7. A stop loss or take profit can't be set as an amount for now, on the order ticket or when you change a position. The ticket shows Amount greyed out with the reason; the position form offers price and pips only and says why. Price and pips work as before.

Prices

8. Waiting orders, Book positions, Live exposure and the Dealing chart show a client's SELL and the current price and profit of a client's open BUY at exactly the price the order fills at.

Assets.NotesMarkdown:
# Backoffice 1.0.107

Sidebar

1. CLIENTS holds Clients, Client requests (KYC, account applications and leverage requests in tabs) and Partners (IB) (partners and payout requests). Each item shows its pending count.
2. CRM holds only the CRM screens, Clients (leads pipeline and Clients 360) and Support tickets, and appears only when the CRM module is on.

Staff permissions

3. New permission Liquidity providers: a manager given it can view and edit the Liquidity providers screen (it was for broker admins only).
4. New permission CRM: it opens the CRM screens. Every existing manager already has it; turn it off on the Staff page to remove access.

Groups

5. The PRICING column names the kind of pricing: Markup, Fixed, Commission / swaps or Mixed, with the number of symbols, or Source.
6. A group's right-click menu shows the group name with its trade handling, without repeating the name.
7. The group Pricing dialog is clearer: a Spread section with Default, Spread markup and Fixed spread as one control, then Commission and swaps, each empty field meaning the default.

Sign-in

8. No "Could not load" message at sign-in on a broker without the CRM module.
